title: Tuga A6 vs Tuga A10: Pocket Handheld or 10 Inch Site Tablet?
description: Tuga A6 handheld (£349) or Tuga A10 tablet (£449), £100 apart. Pocket scanning, photos and sign-off, or a 10.1 inch screen for plans. Or one of each.
summary: The A6 is £100 cheaper, pocketable and has a built-in barcode scanner and a removable battery; the A10 has the 10.1 inch Full HD screen, more memory, a bigger battery and IP68.
lede: If you are choosing between the smallest and largest Tuga Android devices, buy the Tuga A6 (£349) for barcode scanning, proof of delivery, photos and job sheets from a pocket, or the Tuga A10 (£449) to read plans on site. If your firm does both jobs, buy one of each.
verdict: Buy the Tuga A6 at £349 if the job is scanning, sign-off and photos on the move, and the Tuga A10 at £449 if you read plans or drawings on site. The two do different jobs. The A6 is a 277g handheld for a pocket or a belt holster, with a Zebra 2D scan engine built in; the A10 is a 680g tablet for a vehicle mount or a site office, with a 10.1 inch screen at 1920 x 1200 against 6 inches at 2160 x 1080 on the A6. Proof of delivery, stock checks, asset tags, photos and job sheets fit on the A6. Blueprints, PDF plans, BIM viewers and full spreadsheets are easier on the A10.

The £100 buys more than screen. The A10 has 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage against 4GB and 64GB, takes microSD cards up to 2TB against 256GB, and has an 8000mAh battery against 5050mAh. It is sealed to IP68 against the A6's IP67, lists MIL-STD-810H, which the A6 does not, and is rated to 60°C against 50°C. The A6 answers with things the A10 does not list: the integrated Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys, a removable battery so a charged spare can take over mid shift, a 1.5 metre drop rating and Android 15 against Android 14. On paper the cameras match, 13MP rear with flash and 5MP front on both, and both have dual SIM 4G, dual-band Wi-Fi 5 and NFC.

So decide on the work, not the table. If you scan codes or want one device in a pocket, keep the £100 and buy the A6; it is the only Android device in the range with a scanner. If the screen is the job, pay for the A10. The Charging Dock (£49.99) and Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) are listed for the A10 and not the A6, and the A10 has a 3.5mm headphone jack. At 350 nits it is not a bright screen, and the A6 does not list a brightness figure at all, so if you read plans outdoors all day, look at the 1000 nit Tuga A8 at £379 first. Check that the apps you rely on run on the device before you order.
chooseA: Your day is proof of delivery, stock checks or asset tags, and you want a Zebra 2D scan engine built in rather than a camera app: the A10 has no scanner.
You want one device in a pocket or a Belt Holster (£22): 277g against 680g.
You want to swap batteries rather than wait on a charger: the A6's 5050mAh battery is removable, which the A10 does not list (spare batteries are not listed with the accessories, so ask us first).
You want a listed drop rating: the A6 is rated for 1.5 metre drops, and the A10 lists MIL-STD-810H but no drop height.
You would rather keep £100 and the newer Android version: Android 15 on the A6 against Android 14 on the A10.
chooseB: You read drawings, PDF plans, BIM models or full spreadsheets on site: 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 against 6 inches on the A6.
You run heavier apps or keep a lot on the device: 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, expandable to 2TB, against 4GB and 64GB, expandable to 256GB, on the A6.
You want it on the dashboard or in a desk dock: the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) and Charging Dock (£49.99) are listed for the A10 and not the A6. The A6 takes the Car Phone Mount (£17) instead.
You want the higher sealing and the wider heat rating: IP68 against IP67, MIL-STD-810H listed, and -20°C to 60°C against -20°C to 50°C.
You want a stylus for detail work with the gloves off: the Capacitive Stylus (£14.99) is listed for the A10 and not the A6.

faq.q: Is the Tuga A10 worth £100 more than the Tuga A6?
faq.a: If you need the screen, yes, and it is the better specified device in most of the table. The A10 costs £449 and the A6 £349. The A10 has the 10.1 inch Full HD screen, twice the RAM and storage, a bigger battery (8000mAh against 5050mAh), IP68 and MIL-STD-810H, and the dock and vehicle mount are listed for it. The A6 has the integrated Zebra 2D scan engine, a removable battery, a 1.5 metre drop rating and Android 15, and at 277g it fits a pocket. If you scan codes or work from a pocket, buy the Tuga A6; if you read plans, drawings or spreadsheets on site, the Tuga A10 is worth the £100. Both have 12 months of warranty included and can take the paid 3-Year Warranty at £65 each.

faq.q: Should a small firm buy one of each?
faq.a: If your firm does both jobs, yes. The A6 and the A10 do different jobs, so a firm whose drivers or engineers scan, take photos and collect signatures while someone else reads the plans is not choosing between them and needs both. Put the A6 with whoever is on the doorstep, in the stores or in the loft, and the A10 with whoever works from drawings, on the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) or in the cabin. Bulk discounts count devices across models, so one A6 and one A10 qualifies, and the tiers are on the bulk page. The 12V DC Car Charger (£26), the USB-C to USB-A OTG Adapter (£8) and the Tempered Glass Screen Protector (2 Pack, £14) are listed for both devices, so one accessories order covers a mixed pair; see accessories.

faq.q: Can I read drawings on the A6 instead of buying the A10?
faq.a: For a quick look it may be enough; for working from a plan all day, no. The A6 screen is 6 inches at 2160 x 1080. Whether a PDF is comfortable to read for a quick dimension or cable route depends on your own app, so try it on the device. Working through a set of drawings, a BIM viewer or a full spreadsheet means constant pinching, zooming and scrolling, which is where the A10's 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 helps most, and its 8GB of RAM against 4GB gives large files more room. Open the biggest drawing you use on a normal day and see whether you can work from it. Neither is listed as a bright screen for direct sun: the A10 is 350 nits and the A6 does not list a figure. If you read plans outdoors more than indoors, the 1000 nit Tuga A8 at £379 is the one to look at next.

faq.q: Which is tougher, the A6 or the A10?
faq.a: On the ratings listed, the A10. It is sealed to IP68 against IP67 on the A6, lists MIL-STD-810H and tempered glass, and is rated from -20°C to 60°C against -20°C to 50°C. The A6 lists something the A10 does not: a 1.5 metre drop rating. IP67 still covers dust and short immersion in water, so for rain and a dropped device in a puddle both are sealed. The A10 is a slim 14.5mm and 680g, so it is more likely to travel in a bag or a mount than a pocket, and the Rugged Carry Case (£34) suits it; the A6 at 277g rides in a Belt Holster (£22). Our IP rating guide and MIL-STD-810H guide explain what each rating does and does not test.
